messages:
omar: Quick heads-up — during the nightly onboarding batch comparing orion-v2-fp16, orion-lite-int8, and orion-ptq-int4 we saw a weird structured-output ordering flip for funcall responses when streaming is enabled. non-streamed outputs keep the correct array order.

omar: Minimal repro (curl):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.redwood/v1/invoke -d '{"model":"orion-ptq-int4","prompt":"CALL tool enumerate_lines()","stream":true,"seed":2026}'
```

omar: Assembled output recorded:
```json
{"tool":"enumerate_lines","args":[{"pos":0,"text":"first"},{"pos":2,"text":"third"},{"pos":1,"text":"second"}]}
# expected pos order 0,1,2 — note pos 1/2 swapped in output; non-stream run with same seed gives correct 0,1,2
```

tess: interesting. ordering flips but elements preserved? any duplicates or missing items?

omar: preserved, just permuted. happens intermittently ~0.9% on ptq-int4 streaming canary; fp16 baseline under 0.05%.

rui: can you paste raw token boundaries for a failing trace? i.e., per-chunk token-id sequences and where the array brackets landed.

omar: trimmed token/chunk debug below:
chunks=[[60,61,7],[8,9,10],[11,12,13]]
decoded chunks (rough) = ["[ {","\"pos\":0","...","}, {","\"pos\":2","...","}, {","\"pos\":1","...","} ]"]
# looks like the middle item (pos 1) got emitted in the last chunk due to streaming flush ordering

maya: could be emitter flush ordering at the model-kernel boundary or assembly reorder in our stream aggregator that assumes chunks map to top-to-bottom order. did we see any seq gaps?

omar: we didn't have seq headers for this run. i ran a quick mirror with per-chunk seq and it showed seq numbers 1,3,2 for the above run (so emitter reordering likely).

tess: emitter reordering in the PTQ runtime? maybe a parallel tokenizer/decoder thread writing chunks out-of-order when a cache refill happens. does this correlate with kvcache hits/misses?

rui: addendum from token-diff: the ptq-int4 run that reordered had two concurrent prefix batches hitting different KV partitions; the flush path used a separate worker pool which may reorder flush completion. fp16 path uses single-threaded flush in the runtime so it never reordered.

canary-bot: alert: model=orion-ptq-int4 canary: structured-ordering-anomaly 0.92% (baseline 0.04%) link: https://canary.redwood/alerts/6211112222

maya: proposed immediate mitigations:
- add chunk-seq header at the emitter and enforce strict-merge order in the aggregator (maya)
- temporarily disable streaming for orion-ptq-int4 canary until we rule this out (tess)
- replay 50k seeded requests with seq headers to quantify prevalence and surface a minimal repro corpus (omar + rui)
- instrument kvcache hit/miss and worker flush latency per-request to see correlation (rui)

tess: we should also compare kernel selection logs between fp16 and ptq-int4 for these failing seeds. if ptq spawns multiple flush workers to hide latency, we might need an ordering fence.

omar: i'll start the 50k replay now and push results to #eng-ml-results under label=order-flip-probe-621111. i'll include raw seq+chunk payloads for a few tracers.

rui: I'll add per-request worker-id and flush-complete timestamps to the debug build so we can see whether worker scheduling caused out-of-order emissions.

maya: for the aggregator patch, let's be conservative — enforce seq-order but keep a small reordering buffer (50ms) before blocking: helps latency and correctness tradeoff. also add a metric 'reordering_hold_ms' exposed in console.

tess: agreed. disable streaming for the canary for next 4 hours while we collect data. we can re-enable once seq headers + aggregator fix is in place for canary-only.

canary-bot: ticket ML-9817 created: orion-ptq-int4 streaming order-anomaly investigation

omar: note — this was first seen during a benchmark matrix comparing latency/throughput/accuracy across quant modes. surprisingly, ptq-int4 showed a small 0.8% structured-ordering anomaly which would have been catastrophic for downstream function callers. glad we dogfood canary matrix.

rui: timeline: I'll land worker-id instrumentation in ~45m, maya will open aggregator PR for seq-merge in ~90m, omar/ i will run the replay and have preliminary stats in ~2h.

maya: one more thought — add a long-term test in our CI harness: seeded streaming replay that asserts array order for funcall outputs (fail fast). add to nightly regression.

omar: +1. thanks all. will post replay summary when finished. :thumbsup:
